sections.section_name: Section B (Short Answer Questions - 3 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Differentiate between a shadow and a mirror image.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Shadow: Formed by light obstruction; dark region showing only object outline without color or detail. Mirror Image: Formed by light reflection; shows complete color, shape, and internal details of object.

questions.question_text: Describe the practical activity with aim: 'To construct a card pinhole camera and observe real inverted image formation.'. Outline key steps and conclusion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Steps: Make a small pinhole at the center of the outer box's front face., Cut a square window on the inner box face and paste tracing paper over it., Slide inner box inside outer box and point pinhole face toward a bright sunny tree or building.
Conclusion: Light rays from top and bottom of object cross straight through the tiny pinhole, proving rectilinear propagation.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: State the Laws of Reflection, draw a labeled ray diagram, and list four characteristics of images formed by plane mirrors.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Laws: 1. Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane. Image Characteristics: 1. Virtual (cannot be caught on screen). 2. Erect (upright). 3. Same size as object. 4. Laterally inverted (left-right reversed). Image distance behind mirror equals object distance in front.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A student constructs a periscope using a long cardboard tube and two plane mirrors.
Question: At what angle must the two plane mirrors be fixed inside the periscope tube?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The two plane mirrors must be fixed parallel to each other at an angle of 45 degrees relative to the length of the tube, allowing double reflection to view objects above line of sight.

questions.question_text: If a light ray strikes a plane mirror surface at an angle of 35 degrees with the mirror surface, what is the angle of reflection?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Angle with mirror = 35 deg. Normal is at 90 deg. Angle of Incidence (i) = 90 - 35 = 55 deg. By Law of Reflection (i = r), Angle of Reflection (r) = 55 degrees.
